paper_title: Addressable Memory for Video World Models

sections.title: Abstract
sections.content: We study visual persistence in interactive video world models. These models rely on a Key-Value (KV) cache as a growing visual memory to carry forward previously generated frames. However, we find that models can no longer reliably address stored content once rollouts extend beyond the training horizon, because temporal Rotary Positional Embeddings (RoPE) offsets then fall outside the range seen during training and the model struggles to retrieve the relevant visual information through attention. Moreover, naively compressing the cache in the RoPE-rotated space corrupts memory by averaging together incompatible positional phases. To address this, we propose WorldTrace, a training-free memory framework for long-horizon visual persistence. WorldTrace keeps compressed memory addressable by assigning each summary slot a distinct, in-distribution virtual position. Within this addressable cache, we study two memory compression approaches: WorldTrace-Field compresses history for temporal coherence, while WorldTrace-Landmark stores verbatim scene traces at detected transitions for episodic recall. We further introduce LoopBench, a benchmark evaluating whether a compressed cache can reconstruct a previously visited scene after a long detour. WorldTrace-Field improves temporal consistency by +15.5%, and WorldTrace-Landmark improves episodic recall by +19.5% on LoopBench, extending visually persistent generation without retraining.

sections.title: 1 Introduction
sections.content: Memory is what makes generated world persistent. world model should not only predict what comes next, but also preserve what has already been seen. World models aim to simulate worlds we can explore [29, 30, 25], and recent autoregressive video world models [82, 32, 20] pursue this vision by generating video scenes chunk-by-chunk, with each chunk attending over Key-Value (KV) cache of prior context. These models promise interactive applications such as next-generation game engines [84, 20, 32] and closed-loop robot simulators [1, 3], in which users can move freely through visual world and revisit prior locations. Such revisits demand visual persistence, meaning that when an agent returns, the generated results should be consistent with the scenes original appearance, not plausible-looking alternative. In practice, visual persistence degrades rapidly once generation exceeds the training context length. natural way to address this issue is to compress the linearly growing KV cache into fixed-size memory [115, 53, 9, 42] equal to the size of the context seen during training. However, we find that the bottleneck is not simply whether past content is stored in the cache, but whether it remains addressable and how it is compressed. As the generation horizon extends beyond the training context length, the positional encoding these models rely on (e.g., RoPE [78]) is queried at position indices outside its training-bounded range, so the model needs to attend over relative distances that are out-of-distribution (OOD), degrading attention-based memory retrieval. In other words, even if past memories are stored in the KV cache, the model cannot reliably retrieve them. summary placed at such an offset can therefore become hard to reach. This reveals that long-horizon failure is fundamentally problem of addressability, since no memory scheme can improve visual persistence if past observations cannot be reliably accessed once they fall outside the context window. WorldTrace. To tackle this problem, we propose WorldTrace, training-free approach for addressable compressed memory over long horizons. We view this as structured projection of growing visual history into fixed set of retrievable traces. We propose two complementary memory writers: WorldTrace-Field which preserves the coarse field of past information in rotation-invariant space for temporal coherence, and WorldTrace-Landmark which preserves sparse scene-entry traces for long-horizon recall. Our experiments show that addressable memory extends the effective memory horizon. While the sliding-window baseline begins to forget scene structure after only few seconds and loses structural fidelity when revisiting the same location, our WorldTrace maintains consistent scene reconstruction over long rollouts and recovers the original scene appearance  (Fig. 1)  . Our contributions are: 1. We identify two coupled challenges for long-horizon generation in autoregressive video world models, where memory is placed and what it stores. Out-of-distribution temporal offsets make cached tokens hard to address, and RoPE phase cancellation makes naively compressed summaries uninformative (Sec. 2). 2. We propose WorldTrace, training-free approach that keeps compressed memory both addressable and useful without retraining. It assigns each summary an in-distribution virtual position (Sec. 3.1) and organizes the growing visual history into fixed set of retrievable traces, realized by two complementary operators: WorldTrace-Field for temporal coherence (Sec. 3.3) and WorldTrace-Landmark for episodic recall (Sec. 3.4). 3. We introduce LoopBench, memory benchmark of controlled scene revisits that measures whether compressed cache can recover previously visited scene (Sec. 4). We show that WorldTrace extends the effective memory horizon over the default sliding-window cache, with WorldTrace-Field improving temporal consistency by +15.5% on long rollouts and WorldTrace-Landmark improving episodic recall by +19.5% on LoopBench ABA revisits, both without retraining.

sections.title: 2 Rethinking Memory in Video World Models
sections.content: Autoregressive video world models retain prior context as cached keys and values during generation. Longhorizon memory therefore depends both on whether relevant past context remains inside the cache and on whether the model can effectively attend to it during future generation. Two coupled bottlenecks arise. First, cached tokens need to remain addressable (Sec. 2.1), because attending to distant token requires temporal RoPE offset that may lie outside the training distribution, which leaves the token unreadable even when stored. Second, compressed summaries need to remain informative (Sec. 2.2), because naively compressing old keys 2 Addressable Memory for Video World Models lets mismatched RoPE phases cancel out the signal the summary is supposed to carry.

sections.title: 2.1 Position Determines Whether Memory Is Addressable
sections.content: A cached token helps only if the current query can still attend to it. Because tokens temporal RoPE offset from the current query grows with how far back it lies, entries eventually carry offsets beyond the range seen during training, at which point the model can no longer read them even though they still sit in the cache. We summarize the notations in App. A. Concretely, during training the query only attends over bounded range of relative offsets 𝛿𝑞,𝑘 between the current frame and each cached frame: 0 𝛿𝑞,𝑘 = 𝑞 𝑘 𝑡train, where 𝑞 is the absolute position of the current query frame, 𝑘 that of cached key frame, with 𝑘 𝑞 under causal autoregressive attention, and 𝑡train the largest offset seen during training. For temporal RoPE pair 𝑓 at angular frequency 𝜃𝑓 , its contribution 𝑎𝑓 𝑞,𝑘 to the query-key attention score is: 𝑞,𝑘 = Re(𝐴𝑓 𝑎𝑓 𝑞,𝑘𝑒𝑖𝜃𝑓 𝛿𝑞,𝑘 ) , 𝑞,𝑘 where Re() is the real part and 𝐴𝑓 is the content-dependent inner product in canonical coordinates between the query at 𝑞 and the key at 𝑘. During long-horizon inference, these offsets grow ever larger, and 𝛿𝑞,𝑘 can exceed 𝑡train. The affected RoPE components then take on rotation angles the model never saw during training. This effect is frequency-dependent, with the fastest temporal components degrading into positional noise while slower ones stay close to their trained range and keep carrying usable signal [67, 2]. We quantify this per frequency in App. C. Several concurrent methods investigate related positional issues. Infinity-RoPE [107] proposes Block-relative RoPE which reindexes each cached frame relative to the current AR chunk so that 𝛿𝑞,𝑘 always stays within the trained range, keeping generation in-distribution without fixed memory budget. It targets infinite video generation rather than memory compression. Applied to compressed cache, however, this reindexing caps every offset at 𝑡train, so distinct summary slots collapse onto the same position and become indistinguishable (Rem. 1). MemRoPE [42] compresses history into two EMA memory tokens, long-term and short-term stream, which avoids this collapse simply because only two summaries need distinct positions. The design is fixed to two streams and does not extend to an 𝑁 -slot cache, where capped Block-relative positions would again collide. Unlike these, our WorldTrace targets an 𝑁 -slot compressed cache directly by assigning every slot distinct, in-distribution slot-rank position, so an arbitrary number of summaries stay individually addressable at any horizon. We provide detailed discussion of related work in App. D.

Thus we need to keep compressed memory both addressable and informative once generation exceeds the training window. Our WorldTrace is built to satisfy both, which is what lets generated world stay consistent over long, interactive rollouts.

sections.title: 3 WorldTrace
sections.content: We propose WorldTrace, training-free approach for addressable memory in autoregressive video world models. WorldTrace maintains bounded trace of distant history in fixed summary slots via canonical-space key assignment, while keeping each slot addressable (Sec. 3.1). We formulate this cached memory compression for visual persistence as structured sparse attention (Sec. 3.2, App. B). Its two variants, WorldTrace-Field (Sec. 3.3) and WorldTrace-Landmark (Sec. 3.4), target temporal coherence and episodic recall, respectively.

Concretely, the virtual positions assigned to summary slots can diverge from the offset range under which their keys were compressed, so the cached content may no longer match what the query attends to. Block-relative collapse makes compressed entries effectively unaddressable, reducing compression to sliding-window eviction once addressability collapses (Rem. 1). Averaging position-conditioned keys under one offset distribution and querying them under another changes the effective phase of cached tokens, breaking the mean-attention preservation that motivates Def. 2. WorldTrace resolves this coupling by combining two mechanisms. Slot indexing (Def. 1) fixes consistent virtual position scheme, while canonical key averaging (WorldTrace-Field) and frozen landmark keys (WorldTrace-Landmark) absorb the source-to-virtual shift by unrotating keys to canonical space and re-encoding at slot-rank positions. Within this framework, the choice of slot content, averaged frames or frozen landmarks, becomes content-only design choice. We provide the detailed algorithm in App. G.

We evaluate coherence with TempSSIM (, SSIM [91] between consecutive decoded frames) and Local Scene Drift (, mean per-chunk CLIP feature distance to the preceding chunk). For recall, we use Position-Aligned CLIP (PAC , CLIP-ViT-H/14 [70] cosine similarity between geometrically paired returnand forward-leg frames in loops). Baselines. We compare against MG2s default sliding-window cache throughout, which evicts the oldest tokens first-in-first-out with no position correction or content compression, plus controlled variants that isolate position assignment (Block-relative, Centroid-linear, WorldTrace) and content compression (naive vs. canonical averaging, Sec. 4.2, Sec. 4.4). Episodic recall compares three retention tiers (compression, canonical-K anchoring via Latent re-anchor, and verbatim landmarks) on LoopBench and in the PAC sweep (Tab. 3, Tab. 10 in App. E.3). MemRoPE [42], YaRN [67], and Landmark+Block-relative are evaluated in App. E.2. Benchmark. We introduce LoopBench, memory benchmark for scene revisits in AR world models. The model traces waypoints before returning to previously visited location, and the regenerated return frame is scored against the original scene appearance at geometrically matched positions, requiring no external reference. LoopBench varies four properties of the path: waypoint count (𝐾, Fig. 3), rollout length (𝑁 ), camera orientation, and multi-revisit depth (𝑅). The full benchmark gallery with all evaluated configurations is in Fig. 8 (App. F).

sections.title: 5 Conclusion
sections.content: Long-horizon failure in autoregressive video world models is not only matter of retaining more past content, but of keeping that content addressable. We show that temporal RoPE extrapolation can make compressed memories effectively unreadable once rollouts move beyond the training horizon, and introduce WorldTrace, training-free cache mechanism that keeps distant traces at fixed in-distribution virtual positions. Within this addressable cache, WorldTrace-Field provides coherence-oriented summary of history, while WorldTraceLandmark preserves verbatim traces for episodic recall. Empirically, WorldTrace-Field improves Temporal Consistency by +15.5% at 𝑁 = 48, and WorldTrace-Landmark raises Scene Consistency by +19.5% on LoopBench ABA loops, extending visually persistent generation from seconds toward minute-scale return-toorigin rollouts. More broadly, WorldTrace suggests that memory for video world models should be designed around two questions: how to ensure past content remains addressable, and what kind of visual traces should be stored for future queries. The two variants studied here represent different points in this design space, with smooth summaries supporting temporal coherence and sparse landmarks supporting recall of specific places. This perspective also clarifies the limits of the current method. WorldTrace is designed for temporal-RoPE autoregressive models with fixed KV-cache budget, and its current content writers instantiate only two simple structured projections of history, so that WorldTrace-Field favors coherence but can blur specific scene details, while WorldTrace-Landmark preserves specific places but depends on detecting and retaining the right scene 11 Addressable Memory for Video World Models entries. Future memory systems may need to choose these projections more adaptively, especially important in interactive settings where agents move freely, revisit locations, and query the past from changing viewpoints. In this view, WorldTrace-Field and WorldTrace-Landmark are not endpoints, but two structured approximations to the same underlying problem of projecting long visual history into small addressable cache.

sections.title: B WorldTrace as Structured Sparse Attention
sections.content: Under autoregressive decoding with full attention over the history, each new chunk attends to all 𝑇 past frames, so both the per-step attention cost and the KV cache grow as 𝑂(𝑇 ) with generation length. Video world models typically cap this with fixed-size sliding window over the most recent frames. Our WorldTrace instead introduces structured sparse approximations that aim to compress the full 𝑇 -frame history to 𝐿attn 𝑇 effective tokens via projection matrix 𝑃 R𝐿attn𝑇 , where each row defines which frames contribute to one compressed slot. Throughout this section, 𝐾 denotes the canonical (unrotated) key matrix, which is the domain in which the canonical-store operator applies 𝑃 . The slot-rank re-encoding of Def. 1 is applied afterwards at attention time, which is the same fixed, in-distribution rotation on the compressed cache. B.1 Full and Projected Attention For single query 𝑞, the standard attention output is 𝒜(𝑞, 𝐾, 𝑉 ) = softmax(𝑞 𝐾 ) 𝑉 = 𝛼𝑞 𝑉 , weighted sum over all 𝑇 value vectors with 𝛼𝑞 𝑇 , where 𝑇 is the probability simplex over the 𝑇 past frames (non-negative weights summing to one). The projected attention approximation replaces the 𝑇 -token sequence with 𝐿attn 𝑇 prototype tokens (one per compressed slot) defined by row-stochastic matrix 𝑃 R𝐿attn𝑇 , meaning each row of 𝑃 is itself distribution over past frames (this property is what makes the bounds of Sec. B.3 non-vacuous): 𝒜(𝑞, 𝐾, 𝑉 ; 𝑃 ) = softmax(𝑞 (𝑃 𝐾)) 𝑃 𝑉, (5) are the prototype attention weights, now distribution over the 𝐿attn where ˆ𝛼𝑞 = softmax(𝑞 (𝑃 𝐾)) 𝐿attn compressed slots rather than the 𝑇 frames, and 𝑃𝑖𝑉 is the compressed value for slot 𝑖. Relation to prior structured-attention approximations. Eq. (5) is the low-rank factorization of attention studied by efficient transformer architectures, whose projections are learned or trained end-to-end [89, 102, 86, 6, 85, 45]. WorldTrace differs mainly in that the projection is applied training-free at inference time to pretrained models KV cache. Beyond this, two design choices follow from the RoPE-based world-model setting rather than marking contrast with these methods. First, 𝑃 acts in the canonical key domain, so merging avoids the phase cancellation (Sec. 2.2). Second, the compressed slots are re-encoded at slot-rank virtual positions (Def. 1), keeping them addressable beyond the training horizon. The row structure of 𝑃 (uniform averaging for WorldTrace-Field, one-hot selection for WorldTrace-Landmark) then determines whether compression favors coherence or recall, as formalized below. B.2 Structured Attention Approximations Unified by 𝑃 The four cache structures  (Fig. 6)  compared in our experiments correspond to four structured choices of 𝑃 . Sliding window attention. Here 𝑃 = [ 0 𝐼𝐿attn ] makes each row one-hot vector selecting one of the most recent 𝐿attn frames, discarding all earlier history (Fig. 6a). Adding an attention sink anchor is simple modification (Fig. 6b) in which row 0 is pinned to the first (sink) frame while the remaining 𝐿attn1 rows select the most recent 𝐿attn1 frames verbatim, always keeping global context token in cache regardless of generation length. sections.content: Consequently, the compressed representation separates content from position by design, storing only the canonical content average 𝐾 𝑓 in slot whose temporal identity comes entirely from its virtual position 𝑡𝑣. This separation is exactly what slot-rank addressing needs, because the stored content carries no leftover phase from its source timestamps, letting WorldTrace place slot at any virtual position (Def. 1) where query reads the same content. Prop. 2 also pins down this design by showing that any linear operator preserving the mean attention score for every query must output the same canonical average 𝐾 𝑓 , leaving only the virtual position 𝑡𝑣 free, which WorldTrace sets by slot rank (Sec. 3.1). Constraining an operator through the structure of the RoPE rotation it inverts has antecedents in structured-Jacobian parameterizations [57]. One side effect of 𝑀 times averaging is norm reduction, since mutually uncorrelated canonical keys average to roughly 1/ the norm of single key, so summary slot enters the softmax with smaller logit than verbatim key. We keep this behavior rather than restoring the norm with 𝑀 rescale, both because the smaller logit softly downweights heavily compressed history relative to the verbatim recent window and because the rescale did not help at long horizons.

sections.title: D Related Work
sections.content: D.1 Memory-Augmented Transformers Memory-augmented transformers pair recent verbatim window with compressed record of older context, realized as segment-level recurrence with relative positions [19], compressed memory of older tokens [71], external 𝑘NN memory [97], learned memory tokens passed between segments [7, 39], and fused sliding window plus compressive memory [64]. WorldTrace adopts the same two-tier structure, with recent verbatim window plus compressed summary slots. Landmark Attention [63] shares vocabulary with WorldTraceLandmark, but its landmarks are trained representatives that gate attention to off-cache blocks at 1D position, whereas WorldTrace-Landmark is training-free, stores verbatim canonical-frame keys inside the 𝑂(1) cache, and freezes them against unrotate-and-rerotate drift in 3D RoPE. The broader spectrum toward compressed state spans linear attention [40], Mamba [26], and Test-Time Training [80]. We target the fixed-budget, training-free setting in AR video world models. D.2 KV Cache Compression for Large Language Models LLM KV-cache methods fall into three families: window/eviction [4, 98, 115, 53, 9], merging [6, 83], and quantization [56], the last orthogonal to the position-OOD failure we target. DuoAttention [99] splits heads into retrieval and streaming families, parallel to our recent-window and summary-slot split. These methods change content only, picking which tokens to keep or merge rather than which virtual position summary spanning several merged frames should occupy. The closest exceptions touch per-token positional structure [119, 31] or unrotate and rerotate individually retained keys [16, 65], but none reassign summary-slot positions. Our setting also differs from LLM compression in that keys accumulate across independently denoised AR video chunks, so importance must be ranked under denoising-timestep-conditioned queries. Under such queries, angular-concentration scores [61] lose the stable pre-RoPE key geometry they assume, and layer-budget reallocations [9, 114] tune which layers keep tokens rather than how summary slots are addressed at read time. WorldTrace-Field instead averages canonical keys and pairs the result with slot-rank positions. D.3 Position Extrapolation for RoPE RoPE [78] degrades past trained relative offsets. Existing fixes span index rescaling [13, 67, 74], alternative distance biases [69, 81], position-free training [41], and frequencyor content-aware encodings [24, 36], while vision and video extensions add 2D/3D splits [34, 93], camera-relative encodings [50], and training-free diffusion extrapolation [116]. All of this remaps positions for individually retained tokens or fixed-length inputs. Our cache instead needs to be compressed, since fixed 𝑂(1) budget cannot keep every past frame verbatim. Each merged summary then needs an explicit virtual position, quantity that does not arise when tokens keep separate identities, and WorldTrace assigns slot-rank offsets for that role without retraining.

sections.content: Wang et al. [88] tie position to numerical precision, consistent with our coupling thesis (Sec. 3.5). UCM [104] and MosaicMem [111] warp 3D positions for camera-controlled worlds as geometry-driven, trained operators. D.4 Autoregressive Video World Models Interactive AR video world models [25, 32, 20, 84] generate via chunk-wise diffusion prediction, dominantly under the Self-Forcing paradigm [38, 10, 75, 109], which aligns training rollouts with the models own KV cache and inherits local attention window not sized for arbitrarily long inference. Training-time horizon extensions [18, 37] are covered with memory-specific methods in Sec. D.5. Foundation backbones [87] and the world-model lineage from Ha and Schmidhuber [29] through Dreamer [30] to closed-loop driving simulators [3] motivate interactive rollouts beyond passive long-form generation. D.5 Memory and KV Cache for Video World Models Inference-time KV cache. Closest to WorldTrace, inference-time methods modify cache read/write without retraining. Position-side fixes remap or cap temporal offsets via block-relative RoPE with aggressive flushing [107], inference-time position adjustment [17, 47], or per-token virtual positions with cross-frame decay [48]. Content-side writers decide what to merge, prune, or retain, through re-aligned sink tokens [108], dual-rate EMA summaries [42], importance pruning [11, 46], and temporal-correspondence merging [73]. FlowCache [60] targets per-step compute rather than long-horizon recall, but its recent-summary structure parallels ours. These methods adjust the position side, the content side, or pair the two without designing them jointly. To our knowledge, none combines position assignment that keeps an arbitrary number of compressed slots distinct at any horizon with summary writes performed in the canonical pre-RoPE domain. WorldTrace couples exactly these two (WorldTrace-Field compresses, WorldTrace-Landmark freezes), keeping every slot addressable inside fixed 𝑂(1) cache. Training-time extensions. Training-time methods finetune the generator itself for longer effective context. One line pairs partitioned caches or memory hierarchies with RoPE re-alignment or long-context teacher supervision [12, 105, 14, 49, 52, 117, 55]. Memory-decomposition approaches assign different parts of history to dedicated modules [77, 94, 8]. Architectural long-horizon models train for extended rollouts rather than patching fixed checkpoint [27, 66, 79, 112, 120], and Sparse Forcing [103] learns block-sparse attention with persistent anchors end-to-end. Po et al. [68] extend the effective context of video world model with trained state-space memory and evaluate it on Memory Maze with spatial retrieval task, where the model is given trajectory as context and then backtracks the exact action sequence to the starting position. WorldTrace needs no retraining, restoring addressability by changing cache read/write on fixed checkpoint. Geometry-conditioned memory. Trained methods decide what to keep in memory based on camera pose, actions, or scene geometry, drawing on poseand action-annotated compressed latents [35], warped positions or latents for camera-controlled worlds [111, 104, 62], co-visibility-based selection [23], pose-tagged frame re-injection [100], and camera-aware memory gating [28]. WorldTrace is geometry-free, replacing pose-, action-, or co-visibility-driven memory selection with slot-rank positions and canonical cache writes. External memory banks and retrieval. Rather than compressing inside the KV cache, these systems store or retrieve frames outside it and re-inject them via auxiliary attention or re-encoding, through FOV-based frame selection [92], importance-weighted frame contexts [113], first-chunk appearance anchoring [33], cached latent banks [95, 51, 110], and global-state retrieval [15]. WorldTrace keeps memory in the KV cache under one 𝑂(1) recent-plus-summary budget, with no external bank, re-encoding, or retrieval. Comparison. In Tab. 7, we qualitatively compare memory approaches on four axes: whether positional OOD is fixed, whether memory is bounded, whether intermediate history is preserved, and whether retraining is required. For evaluation, WorldScore [21], MIND [106], and VBench-2.0 [118] assess long-horizon quality, and Lian et al. [54] targets revisit consistency in Minecraft. The Memory Maze retrieval task of Po et al. [68] is the closest published revisit test to ours and scores backtracked trajectory against the recorded ground-truth frames, whereas LoopBench sweeps loop topology, rollout length, camera orientation, and multi-revisit depth and scores each return against the models own earlier generation at matched poses, so it needs no ground-truth footage of the revisited scene.

LoopBench: Loop Memory Benchmark We propose LoopBench, benchmark for episodic memory in autoregressive world models. Each task is navigation path that departs from location, visits other locations, and returns. The frames generated on the first visit serve as the reference, and we measure how closely the frames generated on the return reproduce them. LoopBench therefore needs no external reference video, as the rollout itself produces both the target and the prediction. Four properties of the path control task difficulty. (1) Waypoint count (𝐾): the number of intermediate locations between departure and return to (ABA: 𝐾=1, ABCDA: 𝐾=3). (2) Rollout length (𝑁 ): the total number of AR chunks in the path. Longer rollouts put more chunks between the first visit and the return, so the revisited scene sits deeper in the compressed cache. (3) Camera orientation: the agent stays at while the camera pans away by 90, 180, or 360 and then returns, testing whether the initial view is recalled after the pan. (4) Multi-revisit depth (𝑅): the number of times the repeated waypoint is visited in one path (ABABA returns to twice, ABCBA and ABCDBA pass through twice). Each axis varies one property while the others stay unchanged, following the principle that benchmark tasks should be picked to produce distinguishable rankings between candidate systems [58]. We show all twelve configurations in Fig. 8 and evaluate every one of them in Tab. 3. We show qualitative reconstructions on the ABA (axis 1) and pan 90 (axis 3) settings in Fig. 9 and Fig. 10.

sections.title: H Discussion
sections.content: H.1 Limitations WorldTrace operates entirely at inference time, leaving the pretrained weights frozen and changing only what information the fixed-size KV cache retains (compressed summaries in place of evicted frames) and the virtual RoPE positions at which those entries are read, with the goal of improving long-horizon memory. Everything else, including per-chunk visual quality, motion dynamics, and action following, is inherited unchanged from the pretrained backbone. The method also assumes an autoregressive generator with temporal RoPE applied to keys and known local attention window. Compression into fixed budget of 𝑁𝑠 slots is lossy by construction, since each WorldTrace-Field slot averages roughly 𝑇 /𝑁𝑠 frames, ratio that grows with horizon, so frame-level detail inside group is progressively blurred. Under WorldTrace-Landmark, scene can be recalled later only if the scene-entry detector stored it as landmark. Moreover, the cache holds only 𝑁𝑠 landmarks, so rollout that enters more scenes than that loses the oldest ones and can reliably revisit at most 𝑁𝑠 distinct places. Future work could relax this cap, for example by merging evicted landmarks into coarse residual summary slot so that discarded scenes leave recoverable trace, or by selecting which landmark to evict based on predicted revisit likelihood. H.2 Future Directions Geometry-aware canonical keys. Coupling the unrotate/rerotate primitive with camera-pose warping (e.g. the Plücker and Warped-RoPE writers of MosaicMem [111] and UCM [104]) would align frames to shared scene coordinate system and then average, so each summary token blends observations of similar scene content. Learned scene-entry policies. small policy trained on action discontinuities, agent-pose changes, or scene-segmentation logits could let WorldTrace-Landmark commit landmarks during continuous motion and decide which landmark to select. The fixed split between 𝑁𝑠 and 𝑁𝑟 could become an autotunable schedule and adapt per backbone or horizon without the sweep of App. E.5. Fine-tuning extensions. WorldTrace stays within the attention window 𝐿attn, where the budget 𝑁𝑠 +𝑁𝑟 = 𝐿attn keeps every summary slot in-distribution. Two light fine-tuning paths relax this budget. (i) Contextextension fine-tuning on synthetic long rollouts would let WorldTrace allocate more recent slots for coherence or more summary slots for longer recall at the same in-distribution cost. (ii) Position-aware fine-tuning that trains the model on the slot-rank offsets of Eq. (2) would tighten the canonical-mean approximation of WorldTrace-Field. Training memory policies from revisit supervision. The memory policy that decides what to store, compress, and evict could itself be trained, and revisit tasks supply the training signal for free, since whether the model reproduces the original scene on its return is directly measurable. Closed-loop simulators can collect such revisit episodes at scale, supporting supervised fine-tuning on rollouts where recall succeeds as well as reinforcement learning with the revisit score as reward. In both cases the backbone stays frozen and WorldTrace keeps every stored summary in-distribution, so only the lightweight policy over the cache is trained. Scaling LoopBench. We propose LoopBench (App. F) with four difficulty tiers, and it can grow beyond them, since longer paths, more waypoints, and richer camera trajectories are all generated by the same recipe, and evaluating other world models on it would show how well their memory mechanisms support revisits, complementing WorldScore [21], MIND [106], and VBench-2.0 [118]. H.3 Broader Impact WorldTrace is an inference-time cache mechanism that alters no training data, modifies no weights, and expands none of the generative capabilities of the underlying video model, so the relevant considerations are those already attached to pretrained video world models. By keeping long-horizon generation within constant memory budget, it also lowers the compute cost of building on pretrained generators, cost that shapes the wider ecosystem reusing them, from score-distilled 3D synthesis [59, 101] with compute-aware gradient estimators [5, 72] to LLM-conditioned mesh generation [90] and motion attribution for video models [96]. We release no new datasets, and downstream use should follow the base models content policies.
